newsitem.title: USA: Susan McDougal accuses Starr in fresh attack.
newsitem.headline: Susan McDougal accuses Starr in fresh attack.

text.p: Susan McDougal, a former business partner of President Clinton and his wife, has accused prosecutors of forcing her ex-husband into giving false testimony to implicate Clinton in illegal business deals.

McDougal, who is serving jail time linked to the Whitewater investigation, told Reuters in a telephone interview from her Arkansas prison this weekend, that her former spouse James McDougal was meeting with Whitewater investigators every day and buckling under pressure to offer up some dirt on Clinton.

"I think Jim is telling them what they want to hear," Susan McDougal said. "He's very bitter. He's sick and facing 84 years in prison, and when you factor in his grandiosity as a manic depressive, he'll tell them whatever they want to hear to get a better deal for himself."

Susan and James McDougal, who remain friends despite their divorce, were partners of Bill and Hillary Rodham Clinton in the ill-fated Whitewater real estate venture in northern Arkansas before Clinton was elected president.

Targeted by the investigative team of independent counsel Kenneth Starr, the McDougals were earlier this year convicted on a string of fraud and conspiracy charges related to their business dealings from the mid-1980s, including the Whitewater project.
The Clintons have not been indicted but James McDougal is currently talking to Starr's team about the president's business dealings in order to win a favourable sentencing recommendation.

Susan McDougal was sentenced to two years for her part in the alleged conspiracy and is currently serving time for contempt of court because she refused to testify about the Clintons before a federal grand jury.

A witness against the McDougals, former Arkansas loan executive David Hale, testified during their trial that Clinton pressured him to give Susan McDougal an illegal $300,000 loan in 1986, a portion of which was diverted to the Whitewater project.
The McDougals and Clinton denied the charge but Susan McDougal said Saturday she thought her former husband may be reversing his story.
"The prosecutors aren't interested in the truth. They're only interested in hearing someone buttress David Hale's testimony and incriminate the Clintons," Susan McDougal said Saturday.
She and Starr have engaged in a public war of words in recent weeks. The independent counsel flatly denies any improper action in his dealings with the McDougals.
In her latest interview Saturday, Susan McDougal said her former husband, who suffers from arterioschlerosis and manic depression, had despised Starr's team but was now being won over.

"They drive Jim wherever he wants to go. They bring him candy. Jim told me they treat him like a king," she said. "When you're sick and you've lost everything and you're looking at an 84 year prison sentence, being treated like a king has to feel pretty good."

Officials at the Faulkner County jail where McDougal is serving time have asked federal authorities to move her out, arguing that their resources are being stretched by the constant demand for press interviews with her.
Pending approval for her relocation, they have restricted McDougal's press contacts to telephone interviews and barred camera crews from the jail.
